title: On Christian Doctrine
author: augustine
attributionNote: The attribution is recorded as the edition and the scholarly consensus give it; where the attribution is disputed, the work says so.
description: A handbook for interpreting scripture and teaching it. Augustine sets out the distinction between things and signs, the role of the rule of faith, and the claim that love of God and neighbour is the measure of interpretation.
historicalContext: Written in two stages: the first books around 397, the later books around 426, near the end of Augustine's life.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library at read time. Shaw's translation from the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, served by the CCEL.
